The direct fine-tuning setting aligns with Gao et al. (2024), we do a grid search on the number of training epochs, including 10, 15, and 20 epochs for downstream task fine-tuning. The cutoff length is set to 256 and the batch size is 128. For the second instruction-tuning $\rightarrow$ zero-shot tasks evaluation, we conduct instruction-tuning on the MetaMathQA dataset (Yu et al., 2024) for 1 epoch with cutoff length set to 512. We conduct a small hyperparameter sweep within the range of $\beta \in [2.0, 2.5, 3.0]$ , where $\beta$ regulates the standard deviation of experts allocation, as depicted in Figure 6. For all experiments, we use AdamW (Loshchilov and Hutter, 2017) as the optimizer with a learning rate of $3\mathrm{e} - 4$ . ![](images/12e7f38a53aa1a6ec71ee1c8dcd85d5ee9bd788557043d24f7b0ed16ce1c0edd.jpg) Figure 6: The expert allocations for Mistral-7b under different parameter $\beta$ . We apply LoRA experts to four weight matrices in the self-attention module $(\mathbf{W}_{\mathbf{q}},\mathbf{W}_{\mathbf{k}},\mathbf{W}_{\mathbf{v}},\mathbf{W}_{\mathbf{o}})$ and three weight matrices in the MLP module $(\mathbf{W}_{\mathbf{gate}},\mathbf{W}_{\mathbf{down}},\mathbf{W}_{\mathbf{up}})$ .
